events.content: Equinix Q3 2026 revenue total and colocation revenue breakdown

Equinix has not yet filed or reported **Q3 2026** as of October 17, 2026: its investor-relations filing page identifies the latest quarterly filing as the **Q2 2026 Form 10-Q**, filed July 29, 2026, while Q3 earnings are scheduled for October 28, 2026. [[1, 2]] 

In the latest reported quarter, **Q2 2026 (three months ended June 30, 2026)**, Equinix generated **$2.625 billion of total revenue**, up **16% year over year** from **$2.256 billion**. [[3, 4]]

| Q2 2026 segment result | Revenue ($m) | Recurring revenue ($m) | Non-recurring revenue ($m) | Segment adjusted EBITDA ($m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Americas | 1,251 | 1,067 | 184 | 641 |
| EMEA | 845 | 806 | 39 | 456 |
| Asia-Pacific | 529 | 504 | 25 | 299 |
| **Total** | **2,625** | **2,377** | **248** | **1,396** |

The figures above are from Equinix’s Q2 2026 Form 10-Q, which defines the company’s three reportable geographic segments as Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific and reports revenue and adjusted EBITDA by segment. [[4]] 

Americas was the largest and fastest-growing segment, with revenue up **$247 million, or 25% year over year**, to $1.251 billion; EMEA revenue rose **$78 million, or 10%**, to $845 million; and Asia-Pacific revenue rose **$44 million, or 9%**, to $529 million. [[4]] 

For context only, Equinix’s Q2 release guided to **Q3 2026 revenue of $2.525 billion to $2.575 billion**, rather than reporting a Q3 actual result. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Equinix Q2 2026 AI-related leasing xScale demand revenue figures

events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 AI-related leasing xScale demand revenue figures

Equinix did **not disclose a percentage of Q2 2026 leasing/bookings that was AI-related**; management characterized AI qualitatively, saying that the vast majority of its largest deals were AI-workload driven, while reporting total annualized gross bookings of **$424 million**, up 23% year over year. [[1]] [[2]] 

For xScale specifically, Equinix signed **134 MW** of leases across the Americas in Q2 2026, including the Hampton transaction; this is a megawatt leasing measure, not a stated percentage of company-wide leasing or bookings. [[3]] [[1]] 

The identifiable Q2 revenue contribution was approximately **$120 million of non-recurring xScale leasing fees** from Hampton, equivalent to **4.6% of total Q2 revenue of $2.625 billion**. [[1]] [[2]] 

On the reported revenue bridge, Equinix generated **$2.377 billion of recurring revenue (90.6% of total)** and **$248 million of non-recurring revenue (9.4%)**; the company did not publish an exact xScale/AI split of either total. [[2]] 

Thus, the defensible takeaway is: **AI was described as a major driver of large deals, xScale leasing totaled 134 MW, and the disclosed Hampton xScale fee represented roughly 4.6% of Q2 revenue—but no disclosed AI share of total leasing or revenue exists.** [[1]] [[3]] [[1]] [[2]]

events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 interconnection revenue or AI leasing demand split from earnings call transcript

**Q2 2026 takeaway:** Equinix characterized demand as broad-based and stronger than its prior long-term planning assumptions, with demand split between large enterprises modernizing legacy on-premises infrastructure and net-new AI-native workloads/service providers. [[1]]

- Equinix closed **134 MW of xScale leases** in Q2 2026, including the Hampton transaction, which generated roughly **$120 million of non-recurring fees**. [[1]]
- Management said **“the vast majority” of its largest Q2 deals were driven by AI workloads**, consistent with the prior several quarters. [[1]]
- Importantly, the company did **not** disclose that all 134 MW of xScale leasing was AI-specific; the more supportable reading is that AI is a major demand accelerant across its portfolio, while xScale leasing activity includes hyperscale capacity transactions such as Hampton. [[1]]
- The strength translated into a capacity-response plan: Equinix added nine projects since April and had **52 projects underway across 33 markets** at quarter-end. [[2]]
- Q2 revenue was **$2.625 billion**, up **16% year over year**, with growth aided by underlying execution and one-time xScale fees. [[3]]
- Management’s practical demand signal was raised outlook and an accelerated expansion program, with long-term annual capex envisioned at **$5 billion–$7 billion**, excluding real-estate acquisitions and xScale. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** The transcript supports a bullish AI-led leasing thesis—AI drove most large deals and is helping sustain capacity demand—but it does not support equating the full 134 MW of Q2 xScale leases directly to AI demand. [[1]]

events.content: Digital Realty Q2 2026 AI-related leasing demand or revenue

**Q2 2026 takeaway:** Digital Realty did not disclose a separate amount of *recognized AI revenue*, but it did quantify AI-related leasing demand within its small-footprint/interconnection business. [[1, 2]]

- Q2 total bookings were **$307 million of annualized GAAP rental revenue at 100% ownership**, or **$208 million at Digital Realty’s share**. [[1]]
- The **0–1 MW category plus interconnection** contributed **$108 million** at Digital Realty’s share—$88 million from 0–1 MW deployments and $20 million from interconnection—and represented a record level of bookings. [[1, 2]]
- Management said AI-related wins accounted for **roughly 20% of that $108 million**, implying approximately **$21.6 million of annualized GAAP base rent** tied to AI-related leasing in this category; this is an estimate based on management’s “roughly” qualifier rather than a separately reported revenue line. [[2]]
- Management characterized these wins as diverse, generally sub-1-MW/network-oriented deployments, including private-AI and broader service-provider demand, rather than a concentrated large single-customer or single-site lease. [[2]]
- Overall Q2 reported operating revenue was **$1.924 billion**, including **$1.146 billion of rental revenue**, but Digital Realty did **not** identify what share of either figure was generated by AI customers or workloads. [[1]]
- Demand evidence extended beyond the quarter: Digital Realty said it signed two hyperscale leases in July worth **$410 million of annualized GAAP base rent at 100% share** ($205 million at its share), while its Q2-ending backlog reached **$1.9 billion at 100% share** ($1.4 billion at its share). [[1, 3]]

**Bottom line:** AI was a material and growing leasing contributor—about **$22 million of annualized rent implied within the $108 million connected-capacity segment**—but the company’s disclosures do not support treating that figure as Q2 AI revenue or as total AI-related leasing across all Digital Realty product categories. [[2, 1]]

{"deliverable":"Equinix Q2 2026 (three months ended June 30, 2026):

- **Total revenue**: $2.625 billion, up 16% year-over-year from $2.256 billion in Q2 2025. Recurring revenue was $2.377 billion (90.6% of total); non-recurring revenue was $248 million (9.4%). [S1.4]

- **AI-driven leasing / xScale demand**: 
  - Management described AI as a major driver of the vast majority of its largest Q2 deals, consistent with prior quarters. [S6.1]
  - 134 MW of xScale leases were signed in the Americas in Q2 2026, including the Hampton transaction, which generated approximately $120 million of non-recurring xScale leasing fees—about 4.6% of total Q2 revenue. [S2.3], [S2.1]
  - Not all 134 MW were confirmed as AI-specific; AI is reported as an accelerant across the portfolio, with xScale leasing also including hyperscale capacity transactions. [S6.1]
  - Capacity response: 9 new projects added since April; 52 projects underway across 33 markets at quarter-end. [S6.2]

Sources (all cited per requirement):

[S2.3] – Equinix Q2 2026 earnings presentation (134 MW xScale, Hampton fee)
